summary: The Python 2.6 mock library lacks some assert functions but silently passes them, so avoid assert methods marked new in Python 3 docs, verify each assertion by breaking the code, and keep module unit tests Python 2.6 compatible.
questions: Why do my mock assertions always pass on old Python?
Do module unit tests need to be Python 2.6 compatible?
How can I verify my test assertions actually work?

answer_card.title: Python 2.6 traps in mock tests
answer_card.answer_md:
With the Python 2.6 `mock`, missing assert methods don't error, they just look like they passed. So:
- don't use assert functions marked *new* in the Python 3 docs
- run tests under Python 2.6 and break the code on purpose to confirm each assertion fails

Modules (and therefore their unit tests) must stay Python 2.6 compatible.
